profiles._note: profile = 'brief' uses the settings below as they are (SUDAN_PROJECT_BRIEF.md). profile = 'class' overrides them with what the class actually ran on 18 Oct 2026 (QGIS Processing history + the class rule raster, checked cell by cell). Outputs go to output<suffix>, so both can be compared.

dem_class_grid._note: the grid Warp chose automatically for the whole Sudan DEM in class (read from the class redSea_dem_utm36n.tiff). Warping only the Red Sea clip onto this grid gives the same cells without the 400 MB full-Sudan warp. Note: Nearest picks depend on GDAL's warp approximation, which changes with the extent, so this gives about 80 % identical cells, not 100 %.

project.name: redSea_site_analysis
project.question: Northeast-facing, gently sloping land within 5 km of the Port Sudan-Khartoum railway in Red Sea State; site area and population within 5 km.

crs.note: UTM 36N kept for consistency with the course. Red Sea State reaches about 39 E, beyond zone 36 (30-36 E), so planar distances and areas carry a small distortion; Phase 2 reports ellipsoidal $area beside planar area($geometry).

buildings.note: 1.7 M features, about 460 MB; turn on only when needed for the map.

raster.population_margin_note: Margin = catchment 5 km + 1 cell, so catchments of sites near the state border are not cut off.
raster.dem_warp_note: clip_then_warp (brief), use_class_dem (class: the class DEM file, exact and fastest), class_grid (class: Red Sea clip warped onto the class grid, fast, ~80 % identical cells) or warp_then_clip (class: whole Sudan DEM warped first, slow). dem_target_resolution_m null = Warp's automatic resolution.

railway.check_result: Clipped line = Port Sudan -> Haiya -> River Nile border near Berber; 159 features, 420 km, all unnamed (155 narrow_gauge, 4 rail). No Haiya-Kassala branch in this dataset.
railway.network_note: Line ends do not share exact vertices (75 parts at 1 m snap, 6 at 500 m). Fine for Buffer; Option A shortest path needs snapping first.

analysis.invalid_patches_note: 8-connected Polygonize makes polygons whose cells touch only at a corner; QGIS calls these invalid and, with the default Processing setting 'Invalid features filtering = Skip', drops them without a warning. fix = Fix Geometries keeps every patch; skip = drop them, as the class run did (4 sites instead of 15).

wadi_buffer.note: Most redSea_rivers lines are seasonal wadis (flash-flood risk). Land within distance_m is removed from the sites before the area filter.

scoring.normalisation_options: rank = percentile rank 0-1 (robust to one huge site); minmax; log_minmax = ln(1+x) then minmax

road_distance.note: site centroid to nearest road (Join Attributes by Nearest)

rail_distance.note: site centroid to nearest railway; all sites are within 5 km, so keep the weight modest

compactness.note: Polsby-Popper 4*pi*A/P^2: 1 = circle, near 0 = thin sliver. Raster-edged polygons score low but alike.

port_distance.note: site centroid to Port Sudan (export/import access)

buildings_5km.note: OSM building count in the 5 km catchment: a 2026 settlement proxy. Needs vector_layers.buildings.enabled = true and Phase 0 re-run.

scoring.weights_note: Only enabled factors count; their weights are rescaled to sum to 1, so switching one off never breaks the score.

phase3.title: Clicks vs Code: Red Sea Site Analysis
phase3.note: The scoring runs in the browser (same rules as scoring.py). Slope, aspect, corridor and minimum-area thresholds need a Phase 2 re-run.
phase3.roads_note: Web map only: drops 13,800 mostly urban residential/service roads (the road-distance factor uses all roads).

custom_tiles.attribution: Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors; tiles: QGIS Generate XYZ tiles
custom_tiles._note: mode link = relative path to the folder (no copy; only works on this laptop); copy = put the 333 MB of tiles in <dashboard>/tiles so the dashboard folder can travel.

phase3.basemaps_note: The online OpenStreetMap basemap was replaced by the local tiles (custom_tiles): they work offline and use no data. An old 'osm' default now opens the local tiles.
